leads.summary: Open PR #12432 makes the new launcher test fail when both changes are merged
leads.location: test/shell.d/launch-battlenet-test.sh:55-59,62-66; bin/omarchy-launch-battlenet:75-77 (open PR #12432 adds a helper call ahead of line 77)
leads.consequence: #12432 adds omarchy-games-battlenet-scale to the launcher before umu-run. This test only mocks hyprctl, jq, pgrep and umu-run and prepends its mock bin to PATH, not the checkout's bin directory. With both patches applied, the first no-window launch exits 127 under set -e (helper not found), so test/shell and test/all fail on a clean checkout. Add a helper mock to this test or explicitly put the checkout bin on PATH with isolated mocks for any helper side effects. This is a conditional merge conflict, not a failure of #13354 alone.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #12432 open and inserting omarchy-games-battlenet-scale before umu-run (coord/pr-12432.diff), and test/shell adds no checkout bin to PATH; Opus self-check ran a real merge (clean) and got exit 127 without the helper on PATH. Published as related-PR note with inherited-PATH qualifier.

leads.summary: A client with missing class or title aborts the whole jq window scan, but the test's stand-in hides it
leads.consequence: If a preceding Hyprland client lacks class, jq test(null) fails before reaching a later Battle.net record. The error is discarded, WINDOW_ADDRESS becomes empty and the script proceeds to pgrep or another launch. The Python mock replaces absent fields with empty strings and therefore does not exercise the same behavior. Missing title after a nonmatching class similarly errors. Guard nullable fields with // "" and use actual jq in tests covering absent fields. This is an input-edge condition; normal Hyprland records may provide both fields.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus followup-1: Hyprland v0.56.2 always emits class/title as strings (HyprCtl.cpp:402-403,429-430). Unreachable; dropped.

leads.summary: Failed focus dispatches are swallowed and reported as successful launch
leads.consequence: If a matched address goes stale, Hyprland rejects both dispatcher forms, or dispatch fails for another reason, the unconditional '|| true; exit 0' returns success without focusing or starting anything. The desktop entry cannot expose the suppressed error. Return nonzero when both dispatches fail (or fall through to process logic after checking whether starting another process is safe), and assert the fallback and failure cases in the mock.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus followup-1: stale address gives exit 0 in all sibling launchers too; only difference is hidden exit 7 on Lua syntax error of fallback. Not material; dropped.

leads.summary: A matching client without an address is treated as a valid focus target
leads.consequence: For a record whose class/title matches but .address is absent or null, jq -r prints the literal 'null'; the nonempty check succeeds and both dispatches try address:null. The script exits zero without launching even when no process exists. Reject absent/null/empty addresses before treating a record as focusable. This concerns malformed or partial client records, not normal Hyprland addresses.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus followup-1: address always emitted as 0x string (HyprCtl.cpp:387-389). Unreachable; dropped.

leads.summary: Headless refusal provides no visible feedback to desktop-entry users
leads.consequence: The installed app entry runs without a terminal. For a detected running tree with no Hyprland window, the only feedback is stderr while the script exits 0, so a user clicking the app entry sees neither a window nor an explanation. Consider a desktop notification using the project's omarchy-notification-send helper (or another visible UI cue) when refusing the launch.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (finding 1); corroboration only.

limits: No real compositor, Proton, Battle.net or umu process was run. Input-edge repros use mock hyprctl/pgrep/umu-run with a real jq inside review.py; they do not establish frequency of nullable Hyprland fields.

#12432 was simulated by inserting its single new launcher call into a disposable pinned-head copy, not by merging both branches and executing the complete combined tree. Public open-PR state can change.

Also inspected open PR #13195 (configurable Battle.net launch args) touching the launcher. Its added code runs after the new early returns; no separately confirmed failing assertion or actionable merge interaction was found.

flags.claim: A fixed-string check avoids both: `pgrep -af umu-run | grep -Fq -- "umu-run $PREFIX/"`
flags.why: The grep in the same pipeline has 'umu-run <PREFIX>/' in its own command line, so `pgrep -af umu-run` lists it and grep matches itself. With no umu-run process running, the pipeline returned true 200 of 200 times, so the launcher would refuse every launch.
flags.fix: Capture the process list first, then match it: `procs=$(pgrep -af umu-run) || return 1; grep -Fq -- "umu-run $PREFIX/" <<<"$procs"`. Verified: no tree 0/200 (A2), tree running 50/50 (A4), c++dev home 50/50 (A5), battlenet-old sibling 0/50 (A6).
flags.disposition: real error; replaced with capture-then-grep function verified in Opus run3 (A2,A4-A6)

flags.claim: if both land, the no-window launch case would hit `command not found` under `set -e` unless the test adds a stub for that helper
flags.why: Confirmed on a real, clean local merge when the helper is not on the inherited PATH: the test exits 127 with 'omarchy-games-battlenet-scale: command not found' (run3 C1; path.txt shows the helper absent from the sandbox PATH). The test only prepends its mock directory to the inherited PATH (launch-battlenet-test.sh run_launch). On a dev-linked Omarchy machine, env-bootstrap:21-25 prepends $OMARCHY_PATH/bin. On an install that ships the helper, it is in /usr/bin. In both cases it resolves and the real helper runs inside the test instead. So the outcome depends on PATH. The non-hermetic dependency is real either way.
flags.disposition: real error; reworded: clean merge, test calls inherited-PATH helper, exit 127 when none; test scope updated to say local merges

flags.claim: when such a window is listed before the client, or the client is not running at all, the launcher focuses it, exits 0 and never starts Battle.net (reproduced end to end with the browser and terminal cases)
flags.why: Two cases are merged. (a) When the unrelated window is listed before a running client, Battle.net is already running, so the harm is focusing the wrong window, not 'never starts'. That ordering was shown only at the jq level (run1 E-pr-filter-browser-before-client: 0xa returned before 0xb). (b) The end-to-end reproductions were no-client cases: F5 (browser) and F4 (one terminal, the Ghostty-titled window). The foot cwd row was jq-only.
flags.disposition: real error; split no-client (end-to-end: browser, Ghostty rows; foot jq-only) from client-running wrong-focus (jq-only)

flags.claim: The Ghostty row matters because ... Ghostty's shell integration sets the tab title to the running command, which Omarchy's Ghostty config leaves enabled.
flags.why: Lost qualifier. The facts are correct (ghostty.bash v1.3.1:256-259; Config.zig:8613 title=true; args.zig:611 parse starts from defaults; config/ghostty/config:23). However, Ghostty is an optional terminal. Omarchy's default is foot (default/xdg-terminal-exec/hyprland-xdg-terminals.list), which does not set the title to the running command. Without that, readers may assume the default setup is affected.
flags.disposition: real error; added that Ghostty is optional and the default foot does not set the title

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Reviewed at `fc21c17`. **Verified:** the process guard stops a second launch while a tree started by this launcher is running. Two behavior issues remain: the refusal is not visible to someone launching from the app launcher, and the window match also picks up unrelated windows by title. The tests do not exercise the real jq filter or pgrep pattern.

**Verified** (isolated sandbox, mocked `umu-run`, mocked or unreachable `hyprctl`, real `jq` and `pgrep` except where the new test's own stubs are used):

- A long-running process with the command line of Arch's packaged `umu-run` (`python3 /usr/bin/umu-run <…/Battle.net Launcher.exe>`) is matched by the real `pgrep` pattern, and no second `umu-run` starts.
- With no window and no running tree, the launcher starts `umu-run` exactly as before.
- Client classes `steam_app_battlenet` (from `battlenet.lua`) and `battle.net.exe` (from `battlenet.desktop`) are both found. The focus dispatch is the same string the other Omarchy launchers use.
- With Hyprland not reachable, the window lookup returns nothing and the launch proceeds. `--help` and unknown arguments are handled before the new checks.
- The new test passes on its own and under `test/shell`, and fails when the launcher change is reverted.

### The refusal is not visible from the app launcher

When a tree is running with no window (the #13344 case), the launcher prints "Battle.net is already running…" to stderr and exits 0. `battlenet.desktop` runs without a terminal, and the app launcher starts it detached, so that line is not shown anywhere on screen. From the shell's launch feedback code, the user gets "Launching Battle.net…" after 2 s, which clears at 15 s, and then nothing.

**Impact:** in the #13344 situation (hidden to tray, with no usable tray icon), every relaunch is now refused silently, and there is no way back to the running client short of finding and killing its processes by hand. The issue asked to "end the stale tree (or at minimum warn)". The warning exists, but only on stderr.

**Suggested change:** send the message with `omarchy-notification-send`, which AGENTS.md asks for. Its `--exec` click action could offer to stop the hidden copy and start a fresh one. Stopping it automatically is riskier, since a client hidden to tray may be downloading or patching a game.

### The title clause focuses unrelated windows instead of launching

The filter matches `battle.?net` against the class **or** the title, and `head -n1` takes the first hit. With the real `jq` and the PR's filter:

| Client (`class`, `title`) | PR filter | `class` only |
|---|---|---|
| `steam_app_battlenet`, any | match | match |
| `battle.net.exe`, any | match | match |
| `chromium`, `Battle.net - Chromium` | **match** | no match |
| `foot`, `user@host:~/Games/battlenet` | **match** | no match |
| `com.mitchellh.ghostty`, `omarchy-launch-battlenet` | **match** | no match |

**Impact:** when Battle.net is not running, such a window is focused instead, the launcher exits 0 and Battle.net never starts (reproduced end to end with the browser row and the Ghostty-titled terminal row; the foot row was checked with `jq` only). When the client is running but an unrelated window is listed first, the wrong window gets focus (checked with `jq` only). The Ghostty row applies to users who picked Ghostty, which is optional (the default terminal, foot, does not do this): the installer suggests running `omarchy-launch-battlenet` from a terminal, and Ghostty's shell integration sets the tab title to the running command, which Omarchy's Ghostty config leaves enabled. The Ghostty title behavior is from source; its timing was not measured.

**Suggested change:** match on class only. It keeps both known client classes and rejects all three unrelated windows above:

```
select(.class | test("battle.?net"; "i"))
```

`omarchy-hyprland-focus-app` rejects title matches from unrelated windows for the same reason (`hyprland-focus-app-test.sh`).

**Optional test improvement:** the `jq` stub is a Python script that ignores the filter, and the `pgrep` stub ignores its pattern. The shipped test still passed with the jq regex changed to one that never matches, with the jq program made a syntax error, and with the pgrep pattern changed to one that never matches. Using the real `jq` (`require_command jq`, as other shell tests do) and having the `pgrep` stub check that its argument contains `umu-run` and the test prefix would make those cases fail. Asserting the dispatched address would also cover the window choice.

**Pattern edges:** `$HOME` is interpolated into the `pgrep -f` regex unescaped, so with a home directory whose name contains a regex metacharacter, such as `c++dev`, a running tree was not detected and a second copy launched. With no trailing `/`, a tree under `~/Games/battlenet-old/` also matches. A fixed-string check avoids both. Capture the `pgrep` output first, because piping it into `grep` lets `pgrep` list the `grep` process itself, which then always matches:

```bash
battlenet_running() {
  local procs
  procs=$(pgrep -af umu-run) || return 1
  grep -Fq -- "umu-run $PREFIX/" <<<"$procs"
}
```

In the sandbox this returned false with no tree, true with a tree (including under a `c++dev` home), and false for a `battlenet-old` sibling.

**Style:** AGENTS.md prefers a full `if`/`else` to `exit` in one branch, and treats default-package commands such as `hyprctl` and `jq` as always present; the sibling launchers call them without `command -v` guards.

**Related open PRs:**

- #8932 adds its own `battlenet_window_address` and focus block at the same place in the launcher; a local merge of the two heads has a content conflict in `bin/omarchy-launch-battlenet`. Its description says a second `umu-run` "just logs 'another instance is running' and exits", which is the opposite of this PR's code comment about the single-instance lock. Neither claim was tested here.
- #12432 inserts an `omarchy-games-battlenet-scale` call before `umu-run`. The two merge cleanly, but the new test only prepends its mock directory to the inherited `PATH`, so on the merged tree its no-window launch case calls whichever copy of that helper the inherited `PATH` provides. With none on `PATH`, the test exited 127 with `omarchy-games-battlenet-scale: command not found`. A stub for the helper in the test's mock directory avoids both outcomes.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of `fc21c17` against its base, plus umu-launcher 1.4.4 and Arch packaging, Hyprland v0.56.2 and Ghostty v1.3.1 source, and the diffs of open PRs #8932, #10567, #12432 and #13195. The launcher and its new test ran in an isolated sandbox with mocked `hyprctl` and `umu-run` and a umu-run-shaped dummy process. Only the two Battle.net test files ran under `test/shell`, not the full suite. The #8932 and #12432 interactions were checked with local merges of the PR heads. No live Hyprland, Battle.net, Wine/Proton or umu-launcher runs; tray behavior, the client's real window titles, how long a real tree lives and the launch feedback on screen were not observed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
